lessons.title: Pipes and Cisterns: Rates
lessons.concept: Pipes and cistern problems are similar to work-rate problems. An inlet pipe fills a tank at a certain rate, and an outlet/leak empties it. Rates are usually expressed as fraction of tank filled or emptied per unit time. If a pipe fills a tank in x hours, its rate is 1/x tank per hour.
lessons.formula: Fill rate = 1/time_to_fill. Empty rate = 1/time_to_empty. Net rate = sum of inlet rates - sum of outlet rates.
lessons.worked_example: Pipe A fills a tank in 10 hours and Pipe B fills it in 15 hours. Together rate = 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6 tank/hour, so time = 6 hours.
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Combined Pipes and Leaks
lessons.concept: When inlet and outlet pipes operate together, compute net effective rate. If net rate is positive, tank fills; if negative, it empties. Time = 1 / |net rate| for one full tank (assuming constant rates).
lessons.worked_example: Inlet fills in 12 h (1/12), outlet empties in 18 h (1/18). Net = 1/12 - 1/18 = 1/36, so tank fills in 36 hours.
mistakes: Assuming tank always fills when any inlet is open
Sign confusion when leak is faster than inlet
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Partial Filling and Sequential Operation
lessons.concept: Sometimes pipes operate for different durations or open/close at different times. Calculate work done (fraction filled/emptied) in each interval as rate × time, then find remaining work and time needed at the applicable net rate.
lessons.formula: Work done in t hours = rate × t. Remaining = 1 - work done (for filling).
lessons.worked_example: Pipe A (1/8 per h) runs for 2 h: fills 2/8=1/4. Remaining 3/4. If B (1/12 per h) then runs alone: time = (3/4)/(1/12)=9 h.
mistakes: Assuming all pipes run for the full duration
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.
